title: Azure Monitor Alert Rule Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.42 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.42 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" (operationName.value="*scheduledQueryRules*" OR operationName.value="*metricAlerts*")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.42_azure_monitor_alert_rule_42"
| sort -_time
description: Disabled or misconfigured alert rules create silent monitoring gaps; tracking rule state protects on-call coverage.
value: Detecting azure monitor alert rule health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest Activity Log for alert create/update/delete. Nightly compare inventory of enabled rules vs golden baseline lookup. Alert when production-critical rules are disabled > 15 minutes.
visualization: Table (rule, action, caller), Timeline (changes), Single value (disabled rules count).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action span=1h

dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest Activity Log for alert create/update/delete. Nightly compare inventory of enabled rules vs golden baseline lookup. Alert when production-critical rules are disabled > 15 minutes.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" (operationName.value="*scheduledQueryRules*" OR operationName.value="*metricAlerts*")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.42_azure_monitor_alert_rule_42"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect azure monitor alert rule health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_42_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (rule, action, caller), Timeline (changes), Single value (disabled rules count)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure monitor alert rule health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
